title: Contractible fibers and trivial Kan fibrations
statement: Use simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalence, Kan complexes and contractibility as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. A Kan fibration means a simplicial map lifting every horn inclusion, and a trivial Kan fibration means a map lifting every boundary inclusion $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for $n\geq0$. For a Kan fibration $p:X\to Y$, the following are equivalent: $p$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; $p$ is a trivial Kan fibration; every vertex fiber is a contractible Kan complex. For a map $f:A\to B$ of Kan complexes, the mapping-path replacement $P(f)=A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_1}B$ is a Kan fibration; the constant-path map $A\to P(f)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence if and only if all its homotopy fibers are contractible. Here $\partial\Delta^n$ denotes the union of the faces of $\Delta^n$, with $\partial\Delta^0=\varnothing$.
